subject: Mutual action plan: performance benchmarking sprint and windows
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@datacraft.io>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-01T13:12:00-08:00
Subject: Mutual action plan: performance benchmarking sprint and windows

Alex —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our commitment in the MAP, we want to run a focused performance benchmarking sprint next week to validate latency/throughput/TTFT and concurrency for the P0 path (GenerateText endpoint) before the Q4 pilot. Please confirm the items below so we can lock windows: 

1) Success criteria (we proposed in MAP):
   - TTFT (time-to-first-token) median < 200 ms
   - 95th percentile latency < 500 ms
   - Sustained throughput >= 150 requests/sec for 30m windows
   - Concurrency target: 64 concurrent sessions

2) Test environment & accounts needed from DataCraft:
   - Dedicated test harness account (suggested name: datacraft-load-01) with a read-only dataset representative of pilot traffic
   - API test keys and IP allowlist CIDRs for our load generators
   - SRE on-call for allowlist + short troubleshooting window during runs

3) Redwood deliverables before the run:
   - Load scripts (open-source k6 + our generator) and ramp plan
   - Default batching/kv-cache configuration we will try: batching=16, cache-ttl=60s
   - Monitoring dashboard + traces shared link (post-run)

4) Proposed load windows (UTC):
   - Candidate A: 2025-11-10 00:00–04:00 UTC (preferred)
   - Candidate B: 2025-11-11 02:00–06:00 UTC

Attached: MAP-DataCraft-benchmark-plan.xlsx (contains step-by-step checklist and ramp schedule).

Can you confirm that the datacraft-load-01 account + test keys can be provisioned and which window you prefer? If those windows don't work we'll propose alternate nights.

Thanks — I'll update the MAP once we have confirmations.

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Moreno <alex@datacraft.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@datacraft.io>
Date: 2025-11-02T09:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: performance benchmarking sprint and windows

Vanessa —

Thanks, this looks good. TL;DR: we can support Candidate A (11/10) and will provision resources. A few clarifications: 

- TTFT: we understand TTFT as time from request accept to first token byte on the wire. That's fine. Please include the exact header we should capture for precise alignment (we use x-datacraft-req-id).
- Accounts/keys: We'll create datacraft-load-01 and two API keys: dc-load-key-1 (for Redwood load) and dc-sre-key (for smoke). I'll attach the test-accounts csv with account+key placeholders.
- IP allowlist: Our firewall team prefers CIDR blocks rather than individual IPs. We can accept 3 CIDRs for the run; please provide your generator ranges.
- SRE contact: Priya Singh (<priya@datacraft.io>) will be on-call for the window. She asked if Redwood can run an initial 5-minute smoke at least 24 hours before the full window to validate TLS/cert chains and token routing.

We'll attach dc-test-accounts.csv with the placeholders. I confirmed Candidate A for now; if anything changes we'll let you know by 11/07.

Alex
Head of Platform, DataCraft
alex@datacraft.io

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Alex Moreno <alex@datacraft.io>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@datacraft.io>
Date: 2025-11-12T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Benchmark results (11/10 run) + brief MAP update

Team / Alex —

Summary of the 2025-11-10 benchmarking sprint (full run started 00:05 UTC, sustained 35 minutes):

Key metrics (GenerateText endpoint, v1.2.3 model bundle):
- TTFT median: 140 ms
- TTFT 95th pct: 360 ms
- Latency p95 (first-token-to-last-token): 480 ms
- Sustained throughput: 162 req/s (30m window)
- Max concurrency observed: 64 (stable for 24 minutes), small spike at 64->80 caused ~4% 5xxs for 90s during garbage-collection window
- Error rate overall: 0.6% (post-mitigation baseline target <1%)

Notes / observations:
- The GC spike aligned with an unexpected cache eviction pattern. Dylan and infra confirmed the eviction threshold during the run; increasing batching to 32 and raising cache-ttl to 120s reduced the eviction rate on a follow-up short run.
- TTFT and p95 numbers meet our MAP success criteria. Throughput exceeded the baseline target which gives headroom.
- We captured detailed traces and exported them to the shared Drive link. The trace containing the p95 outliers is trace-id: trace-20251110-7a9c (link on Drive).

Attachments: benchmark-results-20251110.jsonl (raw metrics), MAP-DataCraft-benchmark-plan.xlsx (updated with results).

Next steps (MAP checkpoint):
- Redwood to push recommended default config for pilot: batching=32, cache-ttl=120s, kv-cache-size + eviction policy tuned (action: Dylan, due 2025-11-14)
- DataCraft SRE to review traces and mark any request patterns they want re-run (action: Priya, due 2025-11-17)
- Close MAP if both sides sign off on pilot config (tentative close: 2025-11-21)

Thanks everyone — short win for the MAP. If Alex or Priya want a quick readout, we can do a 20-min sync.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
